target.title: fix(matrix): reverse-proxy path support for Matrix homeserver URLs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Matrix channel connections fail for homeservers deployed behind reverse proxies with path prefixes (e.g., `https://host/proxy/base/`). The previous implementation incorrectly constructed transport URLs by using absolute paths, causing `new URL()` to strip the reverse-proxy path prefix and resolve only against the origin.

Users deploying Matrix homeservers in containerized environments, FaaS platforms, or any setup requiring a reverse-proxy path prefix would experience connection failures even with valid credentials and network access.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix moves URL construction entirely to the transport layer by ensuring endpoints are resolved relative to the full homeserver base path. The `apiPrefix` config surface was removed following ClawSweeper review as it was not carried through the runtime (`resolveMatrixConfigForAccount`, `MatrixAuth`, client keying, or `createMatrixClient`), making it a no-op for normal paths.

Key changes:
- `transport.ts`: `normalizeEndpoint()` strips leading slashes so `new URL(endpoint, baseUrl)` resolves relative to the full base path; `performMatrixRequest()` ensures the homeserver URL ends with `/` so it's treated as a directory
- `http-client.ts`: Replaced public `apiPrefix` parameter with private `DEFAULT_API_PREFIX` constant for bare-path resolution only
- Removed unused `apiPrefix` from `MatrixClient` constructor, config schema, and types

This approach keeps the fix minimal and transport-local without introducing new config surfaces that would require migration, validation, and lifecycle management.

## Linked context

- Fixes reverse-proxy path prefix resolution for Matrix channel connections
- No related open issues found
- No known affected releases (config was never shipped)

## User Impact

Matrix channel users running homeservers behind reverse proxies with path prefixes (e.g., `https://host/proxy/base/`) can now successfully connect and communicate. Previously, these deployments would fail during transport URL construction because the leading slash in endpoint paths caused `new URL()` to resolve against the origin only, stripping the proxy path.

No action required from existing users—this is a transparent fix. No new config options were added; instead, an unused `apiPrefix` config surface was removed as part of narrowing the scope.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior addressed**: Matrix channel fails to connect when the homeserver URL includes a reverse-proxy path prefix (e.g., https://host/proxy/base/).
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node 24.13.1, target homeserver (Conduit fork) behind openresty reverse proxy with path prefix at `https://faas-msp.uat.zte.com.cn/faas-function/paas-uat/tuwunel-openclaw-test/`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: 
```
openclaw config set channels.matrix.homeserver "https://faas-msp.uat.zte.com.cn/faas-function/paas-uat/tuwunel-openclaw-test/"
openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --port 18789 --force
openclaw channels status --probe
```
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ![Matrix Channel Status](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7802eb0e-418e-4b58-8022-ee5a2126dd8b)
  ![Matrix Channel Configuration](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/058e949b-862c-4bde-a618-cdf2618e4f60)
- **Observed result after fix**: 
  - `channels status --probe` outputs: `Matrix default: enabled, configured, running, connected, transport:just now, health:healthy, url:https://faas-msp.uat.zte.com.cn/faas-function/paas-uat/tuwunel-openclaw-test/, works`
  - Gateway logs show Matrix plugin successfully connected to the path-prefixed homeserver and joined rooms
  - No URL construction errors in gateway logs
- **Not tested**: Live message send/receive round-trip through the path-prefixed homeserver (relies on homeserver-side routing which is out of scope for this transport-layer fix).

## Tests and validation

- **1393 tests passed** (121 test files) in `extensions/matrix/`
- **New focused test coverage** (2026-07-02): 4 transport tests for path-prefixed URL resolution:
  1. `resolves path-prefixed homeserver endpoint correctly` — verifies `https://host/proxy/base/` + `/_matrix/...` → `https://host/proxy/base/_matrix/...`
  2. `resolves standard homeserver endpoint correctly` — backward compat: `https://matrix.example.org/` unchanged
  3. `handles homeserver URL without trailing slash` — `https://host/proxy/base` still resolves correctly (trailing slash added)
  4. `passes through absolute endpoint when allowed` — absolute URLs are forwarded as-is
- Standard homeserver URLs (`https://matrix.example.org`) continue to work correctly
- No regressions in existing Matrix channel functionality

## AI-Assisted PR Checklist

- [x] AI-assisted (generated with AI coding agent)
- [x] Human-run real behavior proof included above with screenshots and live `channels status --probe` output
- [x] I understand what the code does: `normalizeEndpoint()` strips leading `/` so `new URL()` resolves URLs relative to the full homeserver base path instead of just the origin
- [x] Resolved bot review conversations after addressing them (added real behavior proof, removed unused config surface per ClawSweeper review, added focused transport tests)

## Risk checklist

**Compatibility**: 
- ✅ Config `apiPrefix` was never shipped to any release — no existing users affected
- ✅ Standard homeserver URLs unaffected — backward compatible URL resolution
- ✅ Migration not needed — config surface removed before any release
- ✅ Focused regression tests added covering both path-prefixed and standard URL resolution

**Message delivery**:  
- ✅ Transport-only change — only affects HTTP URL construction, not message formatting or delivery contracts
- ✅ Channel contract unchanged — send/receive/status methods identical signatures
- ✅ Proven pattern — follows same URL resolution pattern used by Discord, Slack, Telegram channel plugins

**Security**:
- ✅ SSRF protections remain fully in place
- ✅ No new config surfaces that could be misconfigured

## Current review state

- Codex review requested real behavior proof and regression coverage — addressed above with 4 new transport tests, screenshots, and live `channels status --probe` output
- All known concerns addressed: proof, compatibility, message delivery safety, regression coverage
